items.rationale: The bicycle was recovered undamaged. Sections 2.3.3 and 7.1.8(c) exclude the entire elective replacement, not just the premium over a standard frame.
The brakes were replaced as part of routine servicing, not to remedy theft damage. Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude the full line.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.8(a) exclude maintenance and tuning unrelated to insured damage.
Under 7.1.10, shipping follows the elective shop work. The invoice does not identify it as transport from the recovery site under 5.2.2(d).
Sections 7.1.8(f) and 7.1.10 exclude attendance charges attributable to the elective shop work, not the separately invoiced recovery.
Sections 7.1.8(a) and 7.1.10 exclude assembly performed for the elective frame swap and service.
Under 3.1.6 and 7.1.10, labour of every grade follows the excluded work it served.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude this hour because it served elective upgrading and servicing rather than insured repair or recovery.

Section 5.2.2(a) covers necessary attendance at the recovery site even though the bicycle was undamaged. At €40 gross, the estimated recovery costs remain below both the €500 mobility cap and the €1,000 recovery cap; no deductible is stated.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers the cutting and removal needed to release the bicycle. Allow €100 gross for the two billed units as one release operation, excluding any labour duplicated on line 11; the aggregate remains below €500.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers necessary recovery labour at about €40 gross for the hour if it is distinct from the cutting charge. Section 7.1.8(g) excludes it if already included on line 10.
